column1: You clean your wounds and apply bandages.
Blessed Rope Belt of the Healer
You feel the elixir course through your veins.
A faint message is inscribed on the band: ''Mary - my eternal love''.
You feel a surge of power as the potion restores your arcane energies.
You are viewing a map. Press any key to continue...
The elixir is bitter and causes you to choke!
This strange object doesn't seem to belong to this world

A historical account of the enslavement of Giants in Thaermore, by Mars Birchun. *The giants of Tharemore, now predominately residing in the Timberland Plains area, are not native to the region of Thaermore. It was the enslavement of these beings for work in the mines that brought them here. *First, a note concerning Giants: they are not the feeble-minded creatures of popular conception. They are, in fact, highly socialized beings equal to that of men or elves, though perhaps their primitive speech patterns and rituals make them appear less civilized. It was this prejudice that led to the giants' enslavement and eventual revolt of the race of giants. *During the late second century, great multitudes of giants were brought from the lands beyond Barrea and forced to work the mines, smashing rock and carrying ore. Their captors thought of them as nothing more than animals and worked them often to their death. However, as their numbers increased, the giants began to secretly organize a rebellion. By the time their captors knew of this plot, the giants had grown too numerous and unified to be suppressed. The revolt of 477 was a bloody uprising that ended with the freedom of the enslaved giants. Hundreds of humans were killed in the rebellion. *Although many to this day harbor ill feelings towards the giants, others now acknowledge the giant's right to freedom and no longer hold them responsible for the bloodshed incurred during the revolt. The giants themselves remain suspicious of humans and choose to stay in the lands they claimed after the revolt, though their numbers have steadily dwindled as many have left to return to their native homelands.

$, *You don't know who I am, but I know who you are. I'm sure you are very confused right now, but you must gather yourself quickly. I've hidden a few basic supplies for you- they are out back near the well. Hopefully you'll remember the secret spot. You need to find a man named Maddock in the village of Aridell, which is just a short walk northeast of here. He'll know who you are and he has been instructed to give you a small package upon your arrival. Be very careful- this land has been befouled and is not safe. If you wish to live, I suggest you stay on the main roads and paths- do not wander! *:E: *The name "Maddock" means nothing to you, nor does the initial "E". With nothing else to go on, perhaps finding this person named Maddock will be your best chance to make sense of this confusion.

A guide to making simple elixirs and potions, by Senior Alchemist Uru Darkfrost. *This lesson book will give you recipes for the four most basic mixtures. All of these potions can be mixed by even the most novice alchemists, except for Keensight which requires just a bit more skill to get the right balance. *For Healing Elixirs and Mana Potions, you'll notice that the more skilled you are in Alchemy, the more potent your mixtures become." *-------------- *Healing Elixir : Willow Sap and Sulfur *Mana Potion : Mandrake Root and Acid *Cat's Eyes Serum : Willow Sap and Bromine *Keensight : Ambergris and Acid

A guide to making complex elixirs and potions, by Senior Alchemist Uru Darkfrost. *This lesson book will cover more advanced elixirs and potions. Most of these mixtures require an Alchemy skill of at least 5 or more. For Healing Elixirs and Mana Potions, review the guide for simple potions and elixirs. *-------------- *Haste : Mandrake Root and Mercury *Ogre Strength : Jelly Fungus and Bromine *Potion of Nimbleness : Jelly Fungus and Mercury *Cure Disease : Belladonna and Charcoal *Detox Serum : Belladonna and Serpent Venom

A guide to making defensive potions, by Senior Alchemist Uru Darkfrost. *This lesson book will cover defensive potions to keep you safe during battle or exploration. Most of these mixtures require an Alchemy skill of at least 5 or more. *-------------- *Leatherskin : Willow Sap and Serpent Venom *Mana Fortify : Mandrake Root and Bromine *Stone Skin : Jelly Fungus and Serpent Venom *Potion of Greater Protection : Ectoplasm and Sulfur *Invisibility : Ectoplasm and Charcoal
"Welcome to the Underground Repository. Validation required for entry. House rules strictly enforced. Trespassers will become permanent guests of the Repository."

(This appears to be a page torn from an old Tome of Alchemy.) *"...would not be recommended under any circumstances. However, one would find that equal parts Willow Sap as a reagent, and Sulfur as a reactant, produces the most effective form of healing elixir. With many years of practice, the talented Alchemist can craft elixirs with properties exceeding that of even..." *The rest of the text is lost below the tear in the page.

This parchment appears to be part of a journal entry... *"After scouting several different areas, I think the pit area is the best place to store my valuables until order is restored in this region. The Salamanders won't disturb the chests and everyone knows best to stay away from this area. Yes! I think the Salamanders will make perfect guards! The invisibility potion will keep me hidden from the beasts until I am finished stashing me belongings...it is common knowledge that Salamanders hunt using sight, not smell. Or is it the other way around? No matter, it will only take me a few moments to place the chests." *There looks to be a crude map of the pit area scrawled under this entry.

You open the book to a page that has been marked: *If everything has been prepared correctly- the Ethereal Salts, the Divining Crystals, and of course the required symbolic Pentagram- you should now be able to activate the circuit via the aforementioned Gateway Incantation. The incantation binds the gates and completes the circuit. If this is your first attempt at creating a Transference Circuit, it is best to make a short distance version in a controlled environment and test it thoroughly to ensure that you missed no instructions. Only after you've perfected the process should you attempt to create one outside your lab. *It is important to remember that a Transference Circuit will remain active, essentially forever, until it has been properly destroyed. The destruction process is complicated and is not covered here. For more information on that, consult Sirus Ortimer's book "Deconstructing Portals and Gateways".

$, *If you are reading this then you have made it safely to Aridell and found Maddock. I could not risk leaving this document with you due to the sensitivity of the information I am about to disclose. I was unsure how long you'd be unconscious and I couldn't risk having this document end up in the wrong hands. Maddock is a simple man who has lived in this village most of his life and I knew he'd be a trustworthy caretaker of this parcel I left for you. Use the gold to buy supplies for yourself- whatever you need to secure your safety and well being. I wish I could have left you more, but it was all I had. *I'm sure you are wondering who I am. My identity will be revealed in time, but for now you should simply trust me. Whether you decide to or not is your choice. *Now, about yourself: you are part of something very big- an event that has affected this entire region. For your safety you were placed into hiding and your memory was erased with a special serum. The name you think you remember, $, was imprinted in your mind. I will not reveal your true name here because of the danger it would bring you, so you should continue to live by the name $. It would be wise for you to not draw attention to yourself by asking too many questions about your past. *Your true identity can be revealed to you but only if you are willing to accept the risk that accompanies it. You must decide for yourself whether to seek the truth or simply become "$" and settle into this new life. If you choose the path of truth it will be a hard and dangerous journey. *And so, if the truth is what you seek, you need to start by retrieving an amulet that belongs to you. Before your memory was taken, you requested that I secure a special amulet for you. I did so by slipping it into the coffin of a recently deceased aristocrat named "Adler Keldam". He is interred in a vault at Eversleep Cemetery in the North Parish region. I knew his casket would be a secure place to hide your amulet; the problem now is retrieving it. The door to the crypt is locked tight. Smashing the door down or picking the lock might be an option, but it may be easiest to just get the key. The cemetery director, Leurik, lives a bit north of Aridell and he has the key. I am confident that you could figure out a way to get it from him. *Once you retrieve your amulet from the crypt, take it to a woman named Lilith who lives in Tangletree Forest. Look for her house in the "heart of the woods". She will tell you what she knows of this amulet and set you on the right path. *Finally, you must use this time to rebuild your strength, stamina and knowledge. You were once very proficient in many skills, which the serum has caused you to forget. Only through experience and practice will you be able to reacquire these Skills you have lost. It is the only way you'll be safe. *:E:

This book talks in depth about the elements of swordsmanship: weapon terminology, proper body postures, offensive and defensive maneuvers, and detailed analysis of legendary sword fights. By the end of the book you know a great deal more about swordsmanship than you did before.

This book talks in depth about the design of locks throughout history: analysis of security features, lock craftsmanship, historical lock designs and lock picking theory. By the end of the book you feel you have a great understanding about the mechanical functionality of locks.

This book is a historical account of how war mauls and hammers have been used in battles since the beginning of time. You learn much about the various designs of bludgeoning weapons, how the most successful warriors wielded them, and even how to splinter every single rib in a man's chest with a hammer strike to the sternum. By the end of the book you are much more learned in the use of hammers than you were before.

This book is a historical account of a Ranger named Tyrus of Blackbarrow. By reading it you learn of his legendary skills with a bow, his techniques for greater accuracy, his opinions on bow designs and arrow variations. In addition to being amused by accounts of Tyrus splitting boulders in two with a single arrow, you gain tremendous insight to the field of archery.

This book is a rogue's guide to using shadow and darkness to conceal your presence. It describes techniques for finding the darkest corners in rooms, using soot to blacken shiny armor and weapons, and anticipating the changing path of shadows cast by moving light sources. By the end of the book you feel as though you have a better understanding of shadow hiding techniques.

This book is a primer to the Elemental realm of arcane magick. It starts by describing the fundamental aspects of the four cosmic elements and how magick employs them. You learn the basics of casting, tips on how to suppress aborted spells, and proper somatic postures for more advanced casting. Although this book was clearly written for novices, you feel you've learned quite a bit about Elemental Magick.

This book is a primer for the realm of Divination magick. It outlines the many gods that are believed to be the source of this magick and how the caster becomes a channel for their divine powers. Likewise you learn various casting techniques for stronger spells, the pros and cons of using dark divination, and the basics of "natural casting" for atheists who study the field of Divination. By the end of the book you feel as if you've learned quite a bit about the realm of Divination magick.

This book talks in depth about the skill of Cartography. By reading it you learn of various techniques for measuring distance and determining world location, direction-sensing underground, avoiding common mapping mistakes and even the complex art of map folding. By the end of the book you feel as if you've learned quite a bit about this subject.

This book is a rogue's field guide to the art of spotting hidden objects in your surroundings. It discusses what features to look for, popular hiding locations for traps and treasure, and techniques for investigating loose stones or suspicious flooring. By the end of the book you clearly have an improved ability to spot hidden features in your surrounding.

This book is a textbook for understanding commerce. In it you learn concepts of bartering and exchange, how to accurately appraise goods, and how to best haggle with a stubborn merchant. By the end of the book your understanding of the business of trade has improved vastly.

This book is a guide to the use of light armors. By reading it you learn of light armor variations, proper care for armor, and techniques for maximizing your armor's protective ability. By the end of the guide you feel as though your understanding of light armor has greatly improved.

This book is a guide to the use of heavy armors. By reading it you learn of heavy armor variations, proper care for armor, and techniques for minimizing the fatigue incurred while using heavy armor. By the end of the guide you feel as though your understanding of heavy armor has greatly improved.

This book covers the history of traps as used for both trickery and warfare. As you page through the chapters you learn of the many designs of traps, their construction and functionality, and of course the best way to disarm a loaded trap. By the end of the book your understanding of skullduggery has increased tremendously.

This book covers the basics of Alchemy. Within the pages you find descriptions of reagents and reactants, mixing techniques for beginners, how to tell when a potion has turned sour, and how to improve the potency of certain concoctions. By the end of the book you feel as though your knowledge of alchemy has improved.

$, *Well done! If you are reading this then you have completed a difficult series of tasks designed to ensure your safety. Although enough time has passed for you to have firmly solidified your new identity, the danger surrounding your previous identity is not completely eliminated. Still, it should be a bit safer now to fill you in on some of the mystery surrounding your past. *First, you undoubtedly see the large gemstone in the box along with this note. Yes, this is the legendary "Crux of Ages" that I'm sure you have heard about. Take it with you and keep it close. It will protect you, but if you show it to anyone it will certainly lead to your death. *Now for how this came into your possession: you found it while scavenging a goblin battlefield looking for valuables. I cannot describe the details of the actual discovery to you now because if it were to trigger memories of the event, your life would be in certain danger. Let me explain: *A powerful Goblin Shaman named Gramuk is using a technique called "Temporal Linking" to locate the person who recovered the Crux. You see, every action you do is etched in your mind as a memory, forever linked to a lifetime of previously accumulated memories. Thus, the event of you finding the Crux was linked to all the memories associated with your prior identity. Scryers who perform Temporal Linking can use these linked memories to identify and locate people by focusing in on specific events. Erasing your identity and all associated memories means Gramuk is unable to connect the event of recovering the gemstone back to you. Even after taking possession of the Crux now, the lack of chronological memories linking you to the gem means it will be many weeks before Gramuk will be able to scry enough information to locate you. *So have you figured out who I am yet? Certainly you must have speculated by now that I am you. Yes, you set this all up to protect yourself- you wrote these notes and devised this scheme to destroy your memory and build a new identity. *Now this is where things get complicated and I will do my best to help you understand what is happening. First, you were not alone when you found the Crux: your brother was with you and shared in the recovery and concealment of the gemstone. He had planned to erase his memory along with you, but he was located and captured by the Goblins before he was able to complete the task. The only chance you had of helping him was to follow through with the plan and erase your own memory first. Now that you've accomplished this, you must locate and help your brother. The Goblins will keep him alive as long as they believe they can extract information from him, but the torture he must be enduring is unthinkable. Days ago, just before you erased your memory, you heard from a Ranger passing through Tanglewood that he may have been taken to the abandoned city Vela, which is now a goblin outpost. *There are many more questions surrounding this war, such as the Chancellor believing that the Orakur have stolen the gem even though evidence strongly points to the Goblins. This evidence, along with the Chancellor's incongruous war plan to abandon security across Thaermore, substantiates the theory that Gramuk is somehow influencing the Chancellor. While you may believe none of this information concerns you, it does, because eventually the Crux will be tracked back to you; eventually your brother will be killed when he is of no more use to the Goblins; and eventually all of Thaermore will fall to the spreading Goblin insurgence. Like it or not, you have become a significant factor in this war. *If you fled now, I wouldn't blame you. You could toss the gem into a river, leave your brother whom you have no memories of to his fate and start a new life somewhere else. However, I know you are stronger person than that. Please, locate and help your brother. He is the only family you have.

Hagbert, *Don't forget: Once you make it to the Lonely Spirits Tavern in Blackwater, you must register under the name "Foozgrumph" for the innkeeper to give you the proper room. Once inside the room, you'll discover that the northwest wall is false. That is how you get there. Don't fail me again Hagbert or I'll cut out your liver."

Gramuk leads you to a large vault just off the main vestibule in his tower room. In the vault you see huge chests filled with gold, gemstones, and priceless bars of Divine Ore. He picks up a canvas sack and begins scooping armfuls of neatly stacked coins from a table into it until the top can barely close. *"With the Crux back in our possession we now have the power to reclaim our ancient homelands. You've aided the race of Goblins, and now I make good on my offer." Gramuk lifts the hefty sack of gold and places it in your arms. "Take this gold, human. It is enough to buy passage out of Thaermore where you can retire as a wealthy lord. But heed this warning: once you leave this Citadel you will be just another human to us. Leave Thaermore and never return." *You cinch the sack of gold closed and hoist it onto your shoulder. It is heavy. Perhaps its weight is more than that of the gold alone, for you realize this sack represents the death of many humans. It represents the lands of Thaermore falling to the Goblin scourge. In time, the weight of this gold may be more than you can bear, but for now your only worry is getting out of Thaermore alive. |add_gold 83510 ; screen_fade_out ; map_port 52 ; move_player 7018 ; screen_fade_in ; areacheck|

Gramuk escorts you through a secret tunnel underneath the Goblin Citadel. He says nothing as he leads you to a small door that he opens and promptly pushes you out of. With the sound of the door closing behind you, you realize it is all over. You stand there against the Citadel wall taking in the events that had just transpired while the desert winds howl and bite your face with sand. Everything happened so quickly that it may be days before the weight of your actions set in. Suddenly, the sound of Goblin war drums carried on the wind bring you back to the matter at hand: leaving this area as quickly as possible. *Under the blanket of the encroaching night, you make your way north to the Nimmia River where you are able to buy passage aboard a supply ship heading northwest into Eschalon.

This book is about a dwarf named Biggins, purportedly the greatest lumberjack who ever lived. He wielded a 45 pound mithril axe and could fell a tree in a single stroke. Within the pages you read of his amazing skills and his tips for keeping an axe razor sharp. A chapter also describes his time serving in the Dwarven Legion of Defenders, where he single-handedly slew 100 mercenary raiders with his axe. By the end of the book you have greatly increased your knowledge of cleaving weapons.

Imbuing your weapons or armor to increases effectiveness is an art going back a thousand years. You will notice that Ectoplasm is the primary reagent needed in all three enhancements: *To increase the damage of a weapon, use Ectoplasm and Serpent Venom. *To increase the armor penetrating ability of a weapon, use Ectoplasm and Mercury. *To increase the protection of armor, use Ectoplasm and Spider Silk. *The important thing to remember is to put these ingredients directly on the object to be imbued; do not mix these in a flask! You must also be skilled in Alchemy to at least level 5 before trying to imnbue any weapons or armor. Master Alchemists of skill 15 or higher achieve the greatest imbuement effects.

This hefty tome recounts the early years of Thaermore's history in exhausting detail. Thankfully, the first chapter is an abridged timeline of events covered within the book. *CHAPTER 1 : An abridgment of historical events concerning Thaermore, eastern province of Eschalon. *--- *Year 390 - Dwarven explorer Koru Keyhammer reaches the Eastern lands known as Thaermore and reports of vast natural resources and deposits of gold, ore and gemstones. *Year 405 - The first permanent settlement called "Loneloft" is established in the mountains of western Thaermore; its founders are primarily miners and surveyors. *Year 409 - Loneloft settlers report they have encountered a peaceful race of subterranean peoples known as the Orakur. They are described as Dwarvish in build but more adapted for permanent life underground, with large eyes and little hair. *Year 419 - Skirmishes arise over control of the mines as the Orakur claim the settlers are stealing minerals from what they refer to as the "Great Underground". By Year 423 these small skirmishes had escalated into war, later to be called The Plague Wars. Dwarven settlers sign an accord absolving themselves from warring with Orakur because of a perceived kinship. Because of this accord, the Dwarven people abandon their claims and leave Thaermore; Thaermore forever becomes predominately occupied by the race of Men. *Year 425 - While mining for copper a settler named Sam of Thorabur discovers a massive gemstone that would become known as "The Crux of Ages". Because of the ongoing conflict with the Orukur the rough stone is hidden away in Bastion Spire, a stronghold which would later become the capitol of Thaermore. *Year 433 - The first governing body of Thaermore is formed. It was decreed that a lifetime Chancellor would be elected to represent the will of people. He is given the highest authority and has a council of twelve advisors, known as The Grand Scholars, serve with him. *435 - Chancellor Marr is elected as the first governor of Thaermore. Under his leadership, Thaermore establishes the Commonwealth Guard, which becomes the turning point in the war with the Orakur. *444 - The Orakur are suppressed and driven deep underground. Chancellor Marr declares victory in the war. The Orakur disappear completely and many assume the whole populous must have succumbed to disease or starvation. Dwarven Lords from outside Thaermore condemn Chancellor Marr for his unethical warfare tactics; relations between the race of Dwarves and Men are fractured. *471 - Chancellor Marr dies after 36 years of distinguished service. Chancellor Marr II, later known as "The Great One", superseded his father as Chancellor. This officially begins the golden age of expansion and prosperity for Thaermore. *509 - Chancellor Torrus I supersedes Chancellor Marr II. *537 - Chancellor Katerra I supersedes Chancellor Torrus I. *[There is an entry here that has been blackened out by ink] *590 - Goblin skirmishes arise in Crakamir. The Chancellor, unwilling to squander resources defending a wasteland, concedes Crakamir to the Goblins. Elsewhere in Thaermore, the Commonwealth Guard is successful in eliminating the Goblin threat. *627 - A devastating earthquake shakes the eastern province, tearing great rifts into the land. The Orakur, long believed to have been decimated, reappear from the great fissures. Surveyors who spot them claimed they appeared skittish and non-hostile. Elusive and rarely seen above ground, the reappearance of the Orakur is not considered a threat and they are all but forgotten. *The timeline ends here, although it looks like the following page may have been ripped from the book.

My dearest sister Penelope, *We have reached the Southern Gates only to find them sealed and with no way to pass into Thaermore. Our caravan leader assured us the gates would be passable, but now we are stuck in Crakamir. Some of the travelers want to return south, others want to stay and find a way north. Either way we are in grave danger if we remain here much longer. *I am writing you this letter in the hope that it reaches you. At daybreak we are going to send someone from the caravan to scout ahead and find a passage to Blackwater. I will give him this letter and instruct him to deliver it to you when he reaches Blackwater. *Sis, I am very fearful. All night we have heard sounds in the darkness. I think our caravan may be encircled, but by what I do not know. We keep the fires burning bright to scare off any creatures, but I think it may be attracting them. *-Mort- |condition (This letter may be of value to this Penelope woman. Do you want to attempt to deliver it to her? Clicking &yes will add it to your quest journal.) (Yes) (No) ; quest 61 1|
Kalus, *Payment will be delivered upon news that William has been eliminated. You are free to do with Blackwater what you want afterwards. *-CM

"Goblin Clans of Thaermore" *Goblins have always been a nuisance to the people of the eastern provinces. Like weeds and mosquitoes, it was a common acceptance that goblins were just here to annoy us, mucking around and causing trouble. Luckily the common goblin is just that- a nuisance that is easily scared away when confronted. Early settlers learned that just keeping a dog nearby or a lantern lit was usually enough to keep the Goblins from stealing chickens at night. *This changed in the late 5th century when Goblins began to organize themselves into clans. Suddenly there appeared Goblin war units capable of causing great harm to others. They stopped being a nuisance and became a danger. During the skirmishes of 590, the Commonwealth Guard experienced noted difficulty in suppressing Goblin raids in the southlands. After securing most of Thaermore, a large wall called the Southern Gate was built to keep the Goblins contained in Crakamir. Human settlers were evacuated from the desert lands. The Chancellor proclaimed it a victory for humans; the Goblins clans claimed it a victory for themselves. *Much was learned of the Goblin war clans at that time. The basic warrior, called the Goblin Hacker, uses a short sword or machete in a savage but effective attack. Goblin Archers have been witnessed to have impressive accuracy with short bows. And the Goblin Bombthug, a unit strapped with a keg of Bangdust, is fully prepared to sacrifice himself in the defense of the unit or a higher officer. Although most Goblins are not known to possess magickal abilities, there are reports of Goblin Shaman among the clan population. *The Goblin unit is loosely assembled and generally led by a Warlord. Warlords answer to a higher officer, usually the clan leader. "Clan leader" is a position held by the strongest goblin; at any time the leader may be challenged and overthrown by a more powerful Goblin.

"The Orakur are watching!" *A collection of scary stories for children. *This appears to be a children's book about Orakur. It is arranged in short chapters that tell tales of Orakur coming up from wells and caves to snatch naughty children away in their sleep. It is accompanied by woodcut images of Orakur, of which no two images appear to match. Some appear small and sneaking, others appear large and menacing. *Although you find the stories amusing, the book contains no relevant information regarding the legitimacy of the Orakur- whether they are real or just a product of fables.

Jak notched an arrow and pulled the string back until he felt that familiar feeling of feathers against his cheek. At that moment he realized he is only at peace when his arm is burning to keep a bow drawn; when he is looking down the shaft of what will be certain death for the next person to enter his sight. *This bow was heavier than what he was used to, with at least 30 pounds more draw. That didn't matter. He felt so focused and alert that he probably could have held twice that additional weight and still have enough accuracy to put the arrow through someone's eye at 100 yards. All the anger and vengeance he had been carrying with him for years was now forgotten. This was the moment he had waited half a lifetime for and he was going to savor every second of it. *In the darkness, far off over the grassy hill that marked the extent of the outpost's defendable area, a soft orange glow appeared on the horizon. Pinpoints of flickering torchlight slowly rose over the crest of the knoll, signifying the approach of an army that was coming to wage war upon the outpost. The front line stretched more than a half-mile wide and through the ground Jak could feel the footsteps of an entire legion of soldiers approaching. 'All this just for me?' he thought to himself as his pressed lips formed into a smile, the first in many years. 'You did not bring nearly enough men with you, dear father.'

Benny knew he shouldn't keep it. If his mother or father found it, they would dash it upon the ground without a second thought and probably give him a lashing that he wouldn't forget for months. *Still, it was beautiful. Dense and leathery, the egg was pleasing to cradle in Benny's arms. It seemed to produce its own warmth, and occasionally Benny felt something inside move. The colors on the egg changed as well, from a spotted purple appearance in the sunlight to a deep green when indoors. And in the darkest of conditions, Benny swore he could see the egg glow faintly from within. Two nights in a row he slept with it under his blankets and it gave him much happiness. He held it close and talked to it, reassuring the egg that he would not let any harm come to it. *By the end of the week Benny noticed a change in the egg. Its shell grew thinner and more flexible, and whatever was inside seemed to grow more restless. Fearful still to tell his parents but having no intention of getting rid of it, he instead kept the egg under his bed in a wooden box filled with straw while he tended the field with his father during the day. This seemed to be a good solution at first, but on the second day Benny returned home to discover something startling had occurred while he was away...

Michael, priest man of Aridell: *You do well and Goblin Lords be pleased. Portal looks to be nearly complete. For final step you must place Ectoplasm and Mercury in the alembic, which should contain the other two components already. This will activate the portal circuit. *I await your success. *-Gramuk

Eschalon, A World of Wonder *Although many dispute the origins of our great world, none can argue its splendor and diversity. Eschalon is divided into 5 great Provinces, with each Province consisting of multiple regions: *The Province of Thaermore, in the east, consists of temperate climates, rolling hills and dense woodlands. A notable area of Thaermore is North Crakamir, home of Eschalon's largest population of Goblins. *To the north and west is the Province of Mistfell. While known mostly for its beautiful coastal regions, it also features deserts in the south. Mistfell is the most populated Province in all of Eschalon and has more cities than any other Province. *The far Western shores of Eschalon belong to Province of Barrea, a harsh wasteland known as The Desolation. This largely uncharted area is known to be home to mercenary clans and giants. The most remote areas of the wasteland are said to be home to colossal beasts. *The far northern region of Eschalon is called the Northland Expanse, an arctic Province of snowy tundra, frozen mountains, and glacial valleys. *The southern Province of Eschalon is called the Rift Zone, a volcanic area of great fissures and rivers of magma. In areas where the volcanoes are dormant and the brimstone has cooled, lush jungles have spread.

The Jewel of Thaermore *The blessed Jewel of Thaermore, to be forever known as the Crux of Ages, was most certainly a gift from the gods. It was found in 425 by Lord Sam of Thorabur while splitting a massive granite bolder in Whispering Cave. Even in its rough form, the stone was a marvelous object, but after polishing the gem was like no other before it. Legend has it that the original gem cutter to work on the stone wept when he gazed at the beauty of the first facet cut. He claimed he saw divinity within the stone. Such a shock was this to the poor man's heart, he died that very night. *The Crux is as old as Eschalon itself, formed under the same circumstances that forge the known world. All of Eschalon's history is trapped inside, and it is believed that those who are in its presence are protected. "What has happened to the Magick Guild?"

"The Magick Guild used to be headquartered in Shadowmirk, the great Mage Hall of the North. After the war began, most of the guild members fled Thaermore. Erubor, head of Shadowmirk, locked down the tower to protect the acolytes who remained there. The defense of Shadowmirk is in their hands now."\n\n"It's not that the guild has formally disbanded, we just have no structure at the moment. There is almost no communication with Shadowmirk now, and the guilds located in Vela and Elderhollow are gone. Here in Blackwater, I sell supplies and training to keep this guild branch open until we can reestablish ourselves."

In this council house stands a man who eyes you suspiciously as you enter.

"Well, well! Greetings to you traveler! I have not seen you 'round Blackwater before, so I assume you are new to our quaint town. I am William, Council Head of Blackwater. I see to the day-to-day operations here, ensuring security to our townspeople during these rough times."

"What is it I can do for you today?"
"So what is it I can do for you today, traveler?" William asks.
"What can you tell me about Blackwater?"

"Blackwater is just an old mining town and nothing more, but not much mining goes on 'round these parts anymore. With the war going on we just decided it would be best to lock the city down. We use the gate tax to support our own militia in case the Orakur try to attack us."\n\n"I know you're just another adventurer that is come to town to buy some supplies and sell some junk you scavenged from a battlefield, so let me give you a bit of advice: you'd be smart to not go snooping around Blackwater too much. We are serious about our security and the guards will be watching you."
"What are your thoughts on this war?"

"This war is about the most absurd thing I have ever come to know. First we are told the Orakur are out to get us, stealin' the Crux and what not. Then, the Goblins show up and start raiding our towns and villages. Now we've got Barrea Mercenaries coming in from the far west, and no one seems to know what they are doing here or what they're up to. I'll tell you, some days I just feel like the whole world is coming to an end. It's only gonna get a whole lot worse before it gets any better."\n\n"I'm sure you were hoping for more information than that, with me being a public official and all, but I really don't know any more about it than you probably do."
"Do you know if there is any work available in town?"

"Well, you can check with the local merchants and see if they have any odd jobs, but you'll find no full-time employment here in Blackwater. Times are tough and even skilled laborers are doing menial jobs just to keep a bit of gold on in their pockets."

"But, since you are looking for work and you appear to have an adventurous spirit, I may be able to offer you a mission of sorts. There have been rumors that a mercenary group has been seeking to assassinate me with hopes of taking over operations in Blackwater. Of course, this cannot be allowed to happen. If you were to investigate this matter and bring me proof of their plot, I could give you a reward."

"Is this something you would be able to look into?"@
"Nothing, I must be on my way." [END]
"That's great. The guards have told me that they have seen suspicious individuals outside the city to the southwest, so you may want to start your search there."
"No, that problem belongs to people of Blackwater, not me."
"Very well. It may be best to not speak of this to anyone else. I don't want the townsfolk to have to worry about such things."
"I have found a note that is evidence of a plot to kill you." [Give William the Mercenary's Note]

"Let me see that." William takes the note from your hand and reads it carefully.

"This is exactly what I feared. Well, I assume you took care of the Mercenaries who held this note. If I could only know who set this hit up!"

"Well, I've got no worries about it right this minute. Here, let me get you a bit of coin from the city's coffer. You deserve this."

You are surprised to see a man apparently living here in the crypt. He appears equally surprised to see you.

"Oh, hello! You startled me. My name is Hesham. I'm sorry, if you are here to visit a loved one, the inner crypt is currently closed. I don't know when, or if, the inner crypt will ever be reopened."

"Now if you'll pardon me for being so rude, I have to ask you to leave. I am currently working on a very important project and don't have time for visitors."

"Well, if you must know, I am working on a project for Leurik. See, we are running out of capacity in our crematorium and he has asked me to come up with a way to mass incinerate bodies. Cremating bodies one at a time in the furnace is just too slow."\n\n"I think I have a formula about finished, but I need a special enzyme that will enhance the scattering property of the combusting fuel. Unfortunately, I just discovered that the enzyme I am looking for is only present in certain insect larvae. I don't have time to gather thousands of larvae needed to extract the few drops of enzyme. I guess I'll have to find an alternate ingredient, but that means the fuel is not going to be nearly as potent. "A
"Yes, so it appears. Look, I need to get back to work. I'm sure you can show yourself out."
"Is there anything I could do for you?"

"Well, I don't know. I need larvae and you don't look like the type of person who would want to spend hours gathering a bag full of larvae for me." Hasham chuckles. "Well, unless you happened to find some very large larvae, then I'd maybe only need 10 or so to get enough enzyme for this concoction."
"Sure, I'll keep my eyes peeled for 'giant larvae' to bring back for you."

"Well, I appreciate your offer. If you bring me back 10 giant larvae I can finish this mixture. I can't pay you any gold for your services, but I could give you a flask of the finsihed Incineration Fuel. I'm sure you could find something useful to do with it."
"I don't have time for larvae gathering. You are on your own."Q
"Uh, yeah. Okay, I need to get back to work. I'm sure you can show yourself out."
"I need access to the inner chamber immediately. I have permission from Leurik."
"I have found 10 Hive Larvae. Can you use these?" [Give 10 Hive Larvae to Hesham]

"Yes, yes! Those will do nicely! Hang on, this won't take long at all."

Hesham takes the larvae from you. At his table, he makes a short incision into each one, exposing a small green bladder. After removing the bladder, he squeezes a few drops of green fluid into a large flask, then swirls it around with some other liquids.

"Perfect! The enzyme has lowered the vicosity of the oils. This will burn splendidly!" He pours about half the liquid into a seperate flask and turns back to you. "Here, take this for your efforts. Be very careful with it because it is extremely volatile. I'm sure you'll be able to come up with some creative use for it."B

Nor'landers hail from the Northland Expanse, an arctic area of permafrost and glaciers.  Nor'landers are of hearty build and are infamous for their ability to survive in conditions where most people would quickly succumb to death. As such, Nor'landers receive a &+2 &Endurance and &+1 &Concentration.

Barreans hail from the vast Desolation of Barrea, far to the West. It is a region of desert and scrubland, where even a simple living requires a great deal of work. Barreans tend to be lean and swift, and can travel immense distances in a short amount of time. Barreans receive a &+2 &Speed and &+1 &Strength.

Rifters hail from the Great Rift Zone of the Under-South, a geologically active area that has been torn into deep valleys and soaring cliffs, covered in a thick forest. Rifters are of slight build and are seldom seen outside the protection of their woods. They are known to be very magickally inclined and claim to have a spiritual connection with the land. They receive a &+2 &Perception and a &+1 &Wisdom.

The Therish hail from rolling woodlands and plains of Thaermore. They are artistic and resourceful people, being expert craftsmen and merchants. The Therish are also well known for their skillful Cavalry. Therish gain &+2 &Concentration and &+1 &Dexterity.

Kessians hail from the coastal region of the Northeast, from Mistfell south along the Cesani Ocean. They are highly regarded as sailors and navigators, and known to be expert tacticians in battle.  They receive &+2 &Wisdom and &+1 &Intelligence.

The Atheist has their mind grounded in observable truths. They simply do not believe in any higher spiritual power or superstitions. Because of this, they are immune to effects of Curses. However, this also makes them immune to the effects of Blessings and altruistic healing from a cleric.

A person of Druidic faith believes in the divinity of the living world itself; plants and animals, sun and rain, day and night. While outdoors, followers of the Druidic faith regenerate lost ^Hit ^Points and ^Mana ^Points much faster than normally possible. However, while in dungeons or underground they regenerate these points much more slowly than normal.

A person of Virtuous faith lives a life of altruism and strives to promote goodwill with others. Their faith often revolves around the worship of one or more deities whom they believe hold dominion over all living things. Virtuous persons automatically receive the spell 'Bless' and can cast it at level one without the need for the *Divination skill. However, Virtuous persons are much more susceptible to being Cursed when in the presence of what they perceive as great evil.

A person of Nefarious faith lives a life of self-indulgence and corruption. By promoting wickedness in this life, they are ensured continued debauchery in the afterlife. Nefarious people have a 5% chance on any attack to deliver 'Malice Damage', an increase in damage gained by the use of savage and cruel combat techniques. However, they are immune to the effects of healing from an altruistic cleric or priest.

The Agnostic person generally believes in some sort of higher power on a personal level, but balances this belief with observable truths and grounded ideals. Being generally balanced, they receive neither bonuses nor penalties.

Fighters are experts at hand-to-hand combat, preferring the feel of a solid weapon in their hand over anything else. Fighters may adventure for the simple thrill of battle, or to sell their services as a Mercenary to the wealthiest armies. The Fighter starts with the *Swords skill.

Rogues are loners who prefers to draw as little attention to themselves as possible. Rogues often develop skills in lock picking and trap disarming, and they may dabble in unscrupulous activities, from petty thievery all the way up to assassinations. Certainly not all Rogues are criminals, and some have even become folk heroes while using their skills to help others. The Rogue starts with the *Pick *Lock skill.

Magick Users are proficient in the Magickal Arts, as either a hobby or profession. Many people claim to possess some kind of Magick talent, but true Magick Users choose to make it part of their everyday life, practicing their art every chance they get. The adept Magick User is both feared and respected by even the mightiest warrior. The Magick User starts with the *Elemental skill.

Healers are people who promote the restoration of life. This doesn't imply that a Healer is opposed to taking life when necessary; sometimes a few must die to save the lives of many. Some Healers work through the use of Divination and spiritual faith, while others live by the sword, insisting that healing cannot begin until the decay has first been cut out. The Healer starts with the *Divination skill.

Rangers are scouts and protectors of their homeland. They are unequaled hunters and survivalists. They fight hand-to-hand in combat only when needed, preferring guerilla tactics and ranged weapons to win battles. The Ranger starts with the *Bows skill.

&Strength is a measure of your character's physical power; his ability to lift and carry weight as well as the maximum force he can deliver when attacking. Nearly all of your Character's physical abilities are augmented by &Strength in some way, including ^Toxin ^Resistance.

&Dexterity is a measure of steadiness, accuracy, hand-eye coordination, balance, and grace in physical activity. &Dexterity is critical in your Character's ^ToHit rating and his base ^Armor ^Rating, as well as skills such as using *Bows, *Thrown *Weapons, and *Picking *Locks.

&Endurance is a measure of how well your character can endure physical trauma, poisons, diseases and fatigue. It is the critical foundation of your Character's ^Maximum ^Hit ^Points and all ^Resistance scores, as well as his ^Hit ^Point regeneration rate.

&Speed is a measure of how quickly your character is able to perform actions. The higher your Character's &Speed is, the faster he can swing a melee weapon (thus increasing maximum deliverable damage) and the lower his base ^Armor ^Rating is because he is more able to quickly evade an oncoming attack.

&Intelligence is a measure of your character's ability to understand and retain new information, as well as his logistic skills. Intelligence also augments ^Element ^Resistance and his ability to identify unknown items. For Magick Users, &Intelligence contributes to the amount of ^Mana ^Point gained every level.

&Wisdom is a measure of your character's insight, common sense and quality of judgment, as well as general cognitive abilities. &Wisdom augments the magickal Skill of *Divination, as well as ^Disease ^Resistance and some defensive stats. &Wisdom is also the only attribute that can protect your character against Cursings. For Healers, &Wisdom contributes to the amount of ^Mana ^Point gained every level.

&Perception is the ability to sense, channel and utilize the arcane energies that exists below the surface of observable reality. In its slightest form, &Perception also affects awareness and intuition. &Perception represents your character's ability to perform acts of magick and divine channeling and is the basis for all his maximum ^Mana ^Points, ^Magick ^Resistance and ^Mana ^Point regeneration rate, as well as their natural ability to spot hidden items.

&Concentration is a measure of your character's ability to maintain attention and mental focus, especially while distressed. It is often considered the mental version of &Endurance. It augments many different Skills and Stats that require strong mental focus and as such it is a critical Attribute to develop for every Character, regardless of his specialization.
The tale told in Eschalon: Book I revolves around a male main character; as such you cannot change this character trait.

This shows the number of remaining ^Attribute ^Points that can be distributed in the Attribute boxes below. Click the Up or Down arrow buttons beside the Attribute to add or removed points. You cannot lower any Attribute score below the base score which you rolled.

This shows the number of remaining ^Skill ^Points that can be used to upgrade your Known Skills. New Skills can be ''purchased'' for #3 #points each from the Available Skills list, or any of your existing Known Skills can be upgraded to the next level for #1 #point each.
Your character's ^Origin grants him certain Attribute bonuses based on which region he hails from.
Your character's ^Axiom describes his basic belief system, which imposes certain advantages and disadvantages to your character.

Your character's ^Class identifies his base proficiencies, interests and way of life. It does not limit his development; regardless of your choice of Class, your character can still evolve in any way you choose and master any combination of Skills. Choosing a Class grants him one predetermined Skill to start out with.
Your character's ^Title is automatically generated based on your ^Axiom and ^Class choices. A Title is simply a denominational label and does not affect character development in any way.

$Click the dice to re-roll your base attributes. Each roll produces a random number between 7 and 14 for each attribute. #Note: this will reset your character and undo any changes you may have made so far.

$Click the NEXT button to select a different portrait for your character. To add a custom character portrait, you must place a $60 $x $60 $pixel PNG file named $mypic.png in the game's installation directory and the game will add it to the selection of portraits.
$Left-click to apply points to a skill. $Right-click to take back skill points applied during this session.

The Arcane Skill of *Alchemy deals with the production of Potions and Elixirs through the mixing of Reactants and Reagents. The higher your skill is in *Alchemy, the more potent a mixture your can create. Master Alchemists may also learn the process of applying these mixtures to weapons and armor, imbuing them with extra abilities.

The Arcane Skill of *Divination deals with Magicks of the Spiritual and Organic realms, used most frequently by Healers and persons of Druidic faith. The higher this skill is, the more powerful of Divination spells you can cast and the lower your chance of spell failure during combat will be. &Wisdom compliments this skill.

The Arcane Skill of *Elemental deals with Magicks of the elemental realms; fire, earth, air and water. The higher this skill is, the more powerful of Elemental spells you can cast and the lower your chance of spell failure during combat will be. &Intelligence compliments this skill.

*Light *Armor encompasses the use of lightweight protection such as soft, hard and studded leathers. The more skilled you are with any armor, the less injury you will receive from a physical attack. Wearing Light Armor on your torso, legs or feet #increases #the #noise #of #your #movement #by #15% affecting your ability to move silently.

*Heavy *Armor encompasses the use of heavyweight protection such as any armor fabricated from metal alloys. The more skilled you are with any armor, the less injury you will receive from a physical attack. Wearing Heavy Armor on your torso, legs or feet #increases #the #noise #of #your #movement #by #30% affecting your ability to move silently.
The *Shield Skill deals with the effective use of hand-held shields in combative situations.

*Cartography is the ability to accurately map your surroundings as you explore. The on-screen automap #does #not #work unless you have at least one point in the *Cartography Skill. The automap becomes more accurate and informative as your *Cartography skill increases.

*Dodge allows you to avoid being attacked through evasive actions, such as a carefully timed sidestep or twist of your body. When you perform a successful dodge, your opponent is thrown off balance granting you a ^+10% ^ToHit probability on your follow-up attack. *Dodge is a passive skill and will be checked automatically each combat round. Your chance of successfully dodging any attack is 1% per point that you have in the *Dodge skill.

*Hide *in *Shadows is the ability to utilize shadow and darkness to cover your movement. It is an automatic Skill that is always active and it grants the effect 'Hidden in Shadow' if your character is in a darkened area. The higher the skill, the less darkness your character needs to utilize this Skill. Also, standing next to a wall or large object increases the effect. &Dexterity complements this skill.
*Lore is the ability to identify the strange items you discover on your journeys. &Intelligence and &Wisdom complement this skill.

*Meditation is the ability to focus your mind to better resist the effects of magickal attacks and extreme elements such as heat and cold. It also allows you to restore your spent ^Mana ^Points at a faster rate.

*Mercantile is the ability to negotiate better prices when buying and selling items from merchants. The higher this Skill is, the cheaper items become when purchasing and the more money you can get when selling items.

*Move *Silently is a stealth skill that allows you to move without producing sound to avoid detection. The higher this skill is, the more it offsets the #penalty #imposed #by #wearing #armor and the closer you can approach an enemy before they notice you. When no enemy can hear you moving, the effect 'Silent' is displayed in the Effects Window. &Dexterity complements this skill.
The *Pick *Locks Skill is the ability to utilize lockpicks to release locks on doors and chests. &Intelligence and &Dexterity complement this skill.
*Skullduggery is the mechanical understanding of traps and trickery, and the ability to effectively disarm them. &Concentration and &Dexterity complement this skill.
The *Spot *Hidden Skill is the ability to passively spot hidden items, doors, traps and abnormalities. This skill is complemented by the &Perception attribute.
*Survival is the ability to dress wounds and utilize common herbs for faster recovery of ^Hit ^Points, as well as an increase in resistance to ^Toxins and ^Disease.

*Unarmed *Combat is the ability to attack a target using only your hands or feet and inflict as much damage as you would if you were holding a blunt weapon. &Strength and &Speed are the attributes that complement the *Unarmed *Combat skill.

*Bludgeoning *Weapons include Staves, Maces, Hammers, Clubs and similar blunt-force weapons. They work equally well at bashing in chests as well as skulls. Bludgeoning weapons are considered melee devices and as such &Strength and &Speed complement this skill.
*Bow *Weapons include any variation of archery devices which utilizes arrows. &Concentration and &Dexterity are the attributes that complement the Bow skill.
*Cleaving *Weapons include Axes, Machetes, and similar chopping weapons. Cleaving Weapons are considered melee devices and as such &Strength and &Speed complement this skill.

*Short *Bladed *Weapons include Knives, Daggers and similar stabbing or cutting devices. Short Swords, being larger and heavier, are considered Swords and not Short Bladed weapons. Short Bladed weapons are considered melee devices and as such &Strength and &Speed complement this skill.

*Swords include all forms of medium to long-bladed, single or double-handed weapons. Short Swords are considered true Swords, not Short Bladed weapons. Swords are considered melee weapons and as such &Strength and &Speed complement this skill.

*Thrown *Weapons include special knives, hatchets and spears designed to be hurled at targets. Thrown weapons will generally cause more damage to a target than other ranged weapons (such as arrows) due to heavier weight and additional inertia, and unlike bows, thrown weapons can be used while holding a torch or shield. The down side is that thrown weapons are heavier in your inventory and more costly per unit than arrows. &Strength and &Dexterity are the attributes that complement the *Thrown *Weapon skill.

This incantation bestows upon the caster a divine blessing, increasing the caster's ToHit and Maximum Damage. The effect of blessing is +1 ToHit probability and +1 Damage per casting level, lasting 100 rounds.
Gives the caster cat-like vision in low light. Duration of spell is 40 rounds per Casting Level.
Removes poisons from the bloodstream of the caster. The higher the casting level, the more powerful the detoxification effect is.
Upon casting, you are bathed in divine light which binds your physical wounds. Heals 3-6 Hit Points for every casting level. Does not cure disease or remove poisoning.
Causes vines and tanglebrush to rise from the ground, ensnaring a target. Spell duration is 4 rounds per Casting Level. Large or very strong creatures may cut the spell's duration in half.
A ranged spell which bathes a single target with divine energy, causing blisters and lesions upon exposed flesh. Effect is 2-4 hit points of Magick damage per casting level.

Causes the skin of the caster to become thick and leathery, increasing the caster's Armor Rating and reducing the effects of physical damage. Casting level determines amount of effect and duration is 100 rounds.
Used to identify unknown items. Effectiveness of the spell is determined by the casting level.
Sprays the target creature with a vaporous mist of toxic fumes, causing the target to become sickened with poison. Casting level determines the potentcy of the poisonous effect.

Temporarily increases the Dexterity of the caster, improving any stat affected by Dexterity such as combat accuracy or base Armor Rating. The effect is +5 Dexterity points per casting level, the duration is 160 rounds.

Temporarily increases the Strength of the caster, improving any stat affected by Strength such as combat damage or encumbrance limit. The effect is +5 Strength points per casting level, the duration is 160 rounds.

Charms a single creature, causing it to turn and fight any other creature attacking the caster. The duration of the charm is 60 rounds. The charmed creature will not follow the caster around, but as long as the charm is active it will attack any other creature nearby that is aggressive towards the caster. The casting level determines the level of creature that can be charmed.

Cures any disease that may be inflicting the caster. Each casting level represents a certain chance for the disease to be eliminated, with the highest casting level (6) being a guaranteed removal of the disease.

This spell, while active, temporarily enchants any weapon placed in the caster's hand. Enchanted weapons deliver an additional 2 points magickal damage upon striking a target. The target may save versus Magick to avoid this extra damage. The spell's duration is 30 rounds per casting level.
Causes the caster to move at increased speed, allowing him to perform an extra action per round. The duration is 4 rounds per casting level.
Casting upon an ememy causes their flesh to rip apart, inflicting 5-7 points of magick damage per casting level.

Causes the skin of the caster to become hard like stone, greatly increasing the caster's Armor Rating and reducing the effects of physical damage. Casting level determines amount of effect and duration is 160 rounds.

Causes an undead target to be repulsed by the caster; at lower casting levels, there is a chance that the spell may fail. At higher casting levels, the spell works every time and additionally may distress the target to the point of causing physical damage as well.

Much like the spell Fleshboil, Massboil causes all living creatures in view (except the caster himself) to be bathed in searing divine light, causing blisters and lesions. The effect is 3-5 points of magick damage per casting level.
The caster lays his hands upon his opponent, channeling a higher power to inflict terrible damage into the target creature. The effect of the spell is 6-10 points of magick damage per casting level.
Removes any curses or hexes that may be plaguing the caster.
Causes some enemies to flee in fright of the magical display of lights. Larger or more intelligent creatures require a higher casting level for the spell to be effective.

Creates a bubble of dense, high-pressure air around the caster, shielding him from most projectiles. Duration is 20 rounds per casting level. Note: Air Shield works only when the source of the projectile is greater than one space away. It does not prevent damage from melee weapons or point-blank (adjacent square) shot projectiles.
Causes a searing hot ember to shoot from the caster's hands towards the target. Effect is 2-4 hit points of fire damage per casting level.
This spell creates a magickal torch that floats above the caster's head, illuminating the darkness around him. The duration of the spell is based on the casting level.
Gives the caster an increased level of protection from elements (fire, cold, electricity). Duration of the spell is 75 rounds and the effect is +10% Resistance to Elements per casting level.
This spell grants the caster +3 points of Cartography Skill per casting level, and the duration of the spell is 10 rounds per casting level.

This spell allows the caster to see the faint electromagnetic aura that all creatures emit, whether they are living, animated or extra dimentional. In daylight this has practically no effect, but in darkness the caster is able to see all creatures glowing green which clearly reveals their location. Using Predator Sight, a caster does not receive any penalty for attacking in low light conditions. Spell duration is 40 rounds per casting level.

This spell creates an intense subsonic wave which temporarily stuns all nearby targets, lowering their combative and defensive abilities. The casting level determines the overall power and range of the blast.
This spell creates a bubble of crushing air around several targets, inflicting 6-9 points of damage per casting level.

This spell, while active, temporarily imbues any weapon held in the caster's hand with bonus fire damage. The effect of the spell is 2 points of fire damage per casting level. The spell duration is 50 rounds.

This spell blasts a single living target with a sub-freezing ball of ice, inflicting a massive 5-8 hit points of freeze damage per casting level. However, the extremely cold temperature generated by this spell has no effect on inanimate objects.

Caster projects a fireball towards his target. Effect is 4-7 points of fire damage per casting level, affecting both living and non-living targets. The concussion of the fireball's blast also produces collateral damage to surrounding creatures and objects.
Causes the caster to blend with the environment, making him harder To hit. Duration is 20 rounds per casting level.

This spell concentrates heat onto the lock mechanism of a door or chest, softening the metal components of the lock and causing them to fail. Higher quality locks require a more powerful casting level as the quality of the metal and craftsmanship of the lock are less susceptible to heat damage.

When cast upon a trap or trapped object, waves of atmospheric pressure compress upon the trap forcing it into mechanical failure. Most traps, especially those of simpler design, are susceptible to these rapid fluxations of pressure and can fail or be remotely triggered through the casting of this spell. The stronger the casting level, the better chance there is of the trap being eliminated. This spell may be cast multiple times on the same trap in effort to disarm it.

This spell allows the caster to set an anchor point anywhere in the world, and then later recast the spell to open a portal back to that anchor point. Each casting level represents a different portal anchor point, so the more locations you wish to anchor, the more Mana it costs to teleport back to that location.

Renders the caster invisible by physically warping light around him, making him completely invisible and impossible to visually track by enemies. The duration of the spell is 5 rounds per casting level.
Supernova sends a fiery blast that emanates from the caster causing 3-4 points of fire damage per casting level on every object and creature in the area.
Find Maddock in the village of Aridell. Aridell is located northeast of where you awoke.

Recover your amulet from the casket of 'Adler Keldam'. His casket is in a crypt located in Eversleep Cemetery in the North Parish area. If you can't open the crypt door yourself, the cemetary director has a key. His house is north of Aridell.
Take your recovered amulet to Lilith 'at the heart' of Tangletree Forest. Tangletree Forest is to the west of the Parish regions.
Farwick, the blacksmith in Aridell, has asked you to recover a bar of Mithril from a wine cellar in the abandoned town of Elderhollow.
Abygale, the magick shop owner in Aridell, has asked you to bring her a book called 'Secrets of Transference Circuits' if you find it.
To release the gates and make Grimmhold passible again, you must open the Secondary Water Gate in Grimmhold's Maintenance level.

Lilith has agreed to give you more information about your amulet, but first you must find and kill the Hive Queen, nesting within a cave in central Tangletree Forest. Her stinger will be proof of her death.

You have discovered that your amulet is actually a key. Take it to the 'Underground Repository' and use it to open lockbox number 26. The Underground Repository may be located somewhere in or around the town of Blackwater.

Locate a 'prize' that the Goblin Gruzz has told you about. Find the Goblin Obelisk in Crakamir, travel south until you see a tree with yellow leaves, then locate the dead tree nearby. The prize is hidden there.

Garrett, the drunk staying at the Owl's Roost Tavern in Aridell, has lost an antique sextant. If you find it, you can sell it for profit or perhaps Garrett would pay more than it's worth to have it back. It may be near the Salted Coast where he washed ashore after the shipwreck.
Leurik has agreed to give you a key to the crypt in Eversleep Cemetery if you eliminate the Salamanders that plague the basement benieth his home in North Parish.
You found a note that says if you register under the name 'Foozgrumph' at the Lonely Spirits Tavern in Blackwater you'll receive a room that has some sort of secret wall in it.

Helpful playing tip: ||Eschalon's game world operates on *Turns. Nothing happens until you take a step or perform an action. Learn to use this to your advantage!
Helpful playing tip: ||Torches on walls can be taken, so don't get caught in the dark without any extras!

Helpful playing tip: ||Click on the Automap window to see the locations you can Quick Travel to. To activate each location, you must travel there and &touch the local marker for that area. After that, you can Quick Travel back so long as you are not in a dungeon or with enemies nearby.

Helpful playing tip: ||When you ready a spell in your Spell Journal, you can hold down a number key 1-5 when you press 'OK' to *Quick *Set that spell. Then you can recall the spell later by just pressing the corresponding number.

Helpful playing tip: ||Wearing a piece of armor without being skilled in the appropriate category still gives you some physical protection, but it reduces your ToHit accuracy and the defensive bonuses you may have acquired through your ^Dexterity and ^Speed.
Helpful playing tip: ||The &3rd &mouse &button or the &W key will enable Walk Lock. Your character will walk in the direction of the cursor arrow until you press any key.

Helpful playing tip: ||When you discover a locked object, any keys in your inventory are tried on the lock. If you have the proper key, the lock will release auto- matically. If you have lockpicks in your inventory, you will be given the option to pick the lock.
Helpful playing tip: ||Hold down the &Left &Shift button while left-clicking on a highlighted object to bash it with your currently held weapon. It's just another way to open locked chests and doors!
Helpful playing tip: ||To cast a *Readied *Spell you must &Right-Click the target. Mac users with one mouse button can hold down the &Left &Control button while clicking.
Helpful playing tip: ||Even the best Mage can't rely on Magick all the time. Consider a minor skill using a melee weapon for when your magick fails you.

Helpful playing tip: ||When you see *Silent in the Active Effects window that means no other creature can currently hear you. If you want to reduce the distance at which others can hear you, increase your ^Move ^Silent skill or stand still by pressing the &Space bar.
Helpful playing tip: ||Demon Oil is a multi-purpose tool...you can injure enemies with it, create barriers of fire, or use it to destroy doors and chests!

Helpful playing tip: ||To rid yourself of an inventory item, you can pick it up from your inventory and drop it into the game window. However, you can also save items by placing them in chests. They will be safe until you return to retrieve them.

Helpful playing tip: ||Bashing objects is very hard on your weapons. Anytime you bash an object you run the slight risk of destroying your weapon in the process, so don't use your expensive weapons to do the job!
Helpful playing tip: ||A spell or potion granting you ^Cats ^Eyes allows you to see in the dark without producing any light. It's perfect for when you are trying to be stealthy.

Helpful playing tip: ||To make ^Hide ^in ^Shadows more effective, stay next to a wall or in a corner surrounded by several walls; this will increase the effect of the Skill. Being surrounded by many trees, especially at night, will also increase the effect of the Skill dramatically.

Helpful playing tip: ||Maximum Weapon Damage is calculated from the weapon itself and your skill with it, as well as certain physical Attributes as follows: Bows use ^Dexterity and ^Concentration; Thrown weapons use ^Strength and ^Dexterity; Melee Weapons use ^Strength and ^Speed.

Helpful playing tip: ||*Mana *Points recover more quickly than *Hit *Points, but if you depend on spells for your survival it's smart to keep a few Mana Potions on hand for instant mana rejunvination.
Helpful playing tip: ||Press the &Tab key to display the tactical grid and highlight enemies that may be hidden behind walls.

Helpful playing tip: ||A switch can be flipped at a distance by throwing something at it, or hitting it with a spell that can damage map objects. Remember, this is the same as bashing, so hold down the &Left &Shift ket to target it.
