You step outside the walls of the dilapidated house and breathe deeply. The air is humid, still saturated from last night's rain. Although you do not recognize the area around you, it seems strangely familiar. The ghostly remnants of nearby abandoned buildings look overgrown and unwelcoming. You stand for just a minute and take it in, hoping that something will trigger an avalanche of memories to crash through and make sense of all this, but nothing comes to you.

You open your eyes. Your head is aching and you immediately realize you have no idea where you are. The only thing you can remember about last night is the terrible storm; the black of night cut with flashes of lightning. *Then you remember something- movement in the darkness. A shadowy presence. Slowly you begin to realize that you have no memory of anything before the storm of last evening. In fact, you have no idea who you even are! It takes much effort before you are able to remember even the most personal information about yourself: your name. *For a moment you are relieved to have remembered anything at all, but alas, your relief is short lived as you look around and assess your situation: you are standing in a strange house in an unknown location having little more than your name in your possession.

The stairs descend into a surprisingly pleasant foyer with fine marble floors. The air is warm and dry, apparently regulated by thermal pipes running under the floors and walls. It is obvious that great effort has gone into ensuring the climate of this place is carefully controlled.

This place seems increasingly familiar to you. Yes, you've been here before. Somehow you know this area. Yet it is strange: as you become gradually more confident that you recognize your surroundings, you feel as if any remaining memories of your own identity seem to be slipping away evermore.

This town has clearly suffered a catastrophic event. Some of the buildings are burned out, others appear to have succumbed to neglect after being abandoned. You notice remnants of war lying about- rusted swords, dented shields, and fragments of bone...

You can feel damp, cool air seeping out from the gaps around the door of this tomb leading you to believe that behind this seal is not merely a tiny mausoleum but rather an extensive underground vault.

This room smells of the blood that has pooled on the cold stone floor. Looking around you see several hooked tools and knives, suggesting to you that this room is used to prepare corpses for internment.
In the center of this room is a large golden statue of a demon. The floor is covered in blood and several humans, apparently victims of sacrificial rituals, lay dead at the base of the statue.

Before you stands an immense steel gate; a large sign has been affixed to it. "NOTICE: The Chancellor of Thaermore has officially closed the gateway to Crakamir and the southern trade routes until further notice." You see a large keyhole in the center of the gate.

This atrium appears to be some sort of a nursery for cultivating these odd purple plants. Shafts of light shine in from windows high above and a complex series of pipes and alembics are circulating water and condensing the secretions that drips from the tentacled branches. A lone person seems to be strolling around this room.

The smell of damp, musty earth fills your nostrils as you descend the stairs into the chilly cellar underneath the abandoned house. You see many long-legged spiders scurrying across the walls and ceiling.

The smell of charred wood and bone hangs in the air here, and the walls are covered in thick soot. This is most certainly a cremation room. Across the floor are scattered bones; anything of value seems to have already been removed from these remains. Ash appears to be overflowing the urns and incinerators.

Inside the vast tower, the air is dry and almost cracks with energy. It smells of books and scrolls; of ancient tomes stashed away in deep libraries. The sweet yet acrid scent of alchemy also hangs in the air, adding to the sense that this place is alive with magick!
This bone storage room is cool and dry. There doesn't appear to be anything of value laying amongst the bones that are mostly separated into various piles.

You are entering a village that is smaller than the deserted one you awoke in earlier. The streets appear to be mostly vacant, yet sounds of life can be heard within the walls of the buildings. You are hopeful that talking to the locals in this town may help you make sense of your situation.

You step into the Grand Hall of Eastern Grimmhold. Even though it has not been properly maintained for some time, the beauty and grandeur of this colossal hall is still impressive with its marble floor and ornate columns. Birds fly freely about due to the lack of a ceiling. Although mostly quiet, you can hear the faint sounds of coughing and gasping somewhere close by.

You step carefully as you descend into the crypt. The stairs, made of loose stones held together by crumbling mortar, shift underfoot. The narrow stairwell opens into a musty hall lit dimly by torches.
These tapestries hanging here display the crest of the Goblin King. It is a sign that this place has been claimed by a goblin clan leader- probably a warlord.

Flipping the switch causes a huge granite block to rise, allowing water to rush down a chute and into a reservoir. As the reservoir quickly fills, you hear pipes creak and groan as the pressures increases. Somewhere, far off in the darkness, the grinding sound of turning gears can be heard.
This area reeks of sewage and the walls seem to move with hundreds of cockroaches. You promptly cover your mouth and nose so as not to breathe in the filthy air.

The air in this chamber is heavy and sour. The floor is covered in soft, moist dung crawling with beetles. In the darkness above you, you hear a cacophony of shrill screeches...bats. It would be best not to disturb anything here.
Something wedged in the loose rocks catches your eye. Perhaps something was carried in here by the bats and dropped  into these rocks.

It looks as if this area has been blasted shut. You can hear air whistling through the tunnels on the other side of the rock pile. It looks as if this was an attempt to seal the deeper sections of the cave off to prevent anything from getting in, or out.

What is this? A strange set of levers so deep in this remote cave! Perhaps they operate old mining equipment that was long ago abandoned, or maybe when manipulated correctly they open a secret door to a thieves' lair. There is only one way to find out...
Faint light seeps in from above; it's just enough to allow a few twisted shrubs and trees to take root  in this damp and chilly cave.

The entrance to the Ossuary seems to have been destroyed, probably kicked in by thieves trying to gain entry. However, you find it a bit disconcerting that the remains of the door actually appear to broken outward and now lay about the yard. From here you see that the entry hall into the Ossuary is a gradually descending slope that disappears into pitch darkness deep underground.

This tavern is small and nearly empty. The owner sees you enter and quickly begins to wipe off a table, apparently trying to appear busy. In the corner a man sits at a table drinking from a bottle of whiskey.
The southwest gate to Blackwater appears to be overgrown and unused.
Something is not right here. The air seems strangely still. You feel as if the trees themselves are watching you...

You realize you are walking among the remnants of a battlefield. Suddenly you are hit with the most powerful memory since your journey began! This place- this battlefield- feels incredibly familiar, yet you cannot hold onto these memories as they rapidly slip away. Then, just as quickly as the faint memories appeared, they are gone.

This tiny house is nearly empty except for trash and debris scattered about. It smells of death in this room, and you quickly notice a decomposing body laying at the back of the room in a pool of thick, congealed blood.

Your eye catches something odd about the northwest wall of this room. A small section of the wall seems slightly misaligned. Upon touching it you discover that it is just an illusion...your hand passes through it as freely as if it wasn't there.
This room appears to be filled with dozens of shallow, unmarked graves. The air here is very damp and cold. Centipedes and worms wriggle through the overturned soil at your feet.

As you approach the tiny overgrown house, you notice a row of powder kegs partially blocking the path leading up to the missing front door. A rudimentary flint and steel trap seems to be rigged to one of the barrels and a pull cord runs along the ground and into the house. Upon closer inspection you see that the powder kegs are waterlogged and rotting; the chances of them exploding are very slim, if they even contain any powder at all. From here you can see a person inside the house, apparently unaware of your presence.

You enter this small antechamber and see it is in a state of chaos. Chairs lay strewn about, a broken table lies splintered on the floor, and a rotting corpse lies in the corner. This room appears to have been a meeting area at one time, but now it is little more than the filthy tomb of a mediocre thief. How he met his fate is a mystery.
Broken wine racks and bottles lie everywhere. It appears that any wine of value has already been taken or unfortunately smashed upon the ground.
This is a killing ground. Bodies of varying stages of decomposition lie about, striped of their valuables. It is clear that these thieves hold no respect or sympathy for their victims.

Before you stands the sealed front gates of a foreboding, dark tower. It's a strikingly large structure adorned with strange archaic symbols. You notice that the entire building has been built out over the water; only the front entrance seems to be connected to the land. From here you do not see any way to operate the front gates other than a switch in the inner yard, which is completely unreachable.

At the entrance of this cave you hear the air rushing out over the jagged rocks, creating a whistling noise that grows to a howl when the wind increases. You notice footprints in the soft red clay of the cave's floor, though it is impossible to tell how long they've been there.

Here you notice that the ground is littered with the unmistakable remnants of a goblin camp: the bones of small animals, a rusted dagger whose blade has been bent beyond use, and the foul stench of rotten meat and fermented weed juice. Yes, Goblins have passed through here recently and probably rested in this spot.
Aha! A back entrance to the dark tower! And better yet, the door appears to be slightly ajar as if it were not properly closed the last time someone used it.
You begin to smell the foul stench of an animal enclosure that seems to have not been cleaned for quite a while. Mold grows thick on the walls in this area.
The door opens to reveal a pit with a ladder leading to the darkness below. You are instantly struck by the acidic smell of alchemy rising from the hole.
This appears to be some sort of magickal platform used in the casting of specific spells. It is overgrown and dirty as if it has not been used in a long while.

The horror! These bodies have been shredded by ravenous beasts. Entrails lay about, pulled from their bodies and partially consumed. Bits of hair and skin appear to even be hanging in the surrounding shrubbery and trees. The death these men must have experienced is unfathomable.

You step into a massive domed pit. A single shaft of light high above is the only illumination in this depressing abode. Fragments of bone lay scattered everywhere and are easily crushed into dust beneath your feet. This is an oubliette; a place of death and suffering, a place where many unfortunate souls were cast, where they anguished for days in absolute darkness while centipedes and cockroaches ate them alive. It seems as if their tormented cries still echo from through the darkness.

You are entering the town of Vela. A ghostly fog hangs in the air and most of the streets appear to be flooded with water. On this main avenue entering the town, banners displaying the goblin crest are nailed to makeshift walls, built from the ruins of the once bustling shops. You also see Goblin totems- long poles adorned with human skulls. These are territorial signs. This area belongs to the goblins now.
This is a heavy, impassible gate. There is neither a keyhole nor any visible method of operation. It almost looks as if this gate was never intended to be opened.
The remnants of a road sign lies strewn upon the ground. It looks like it was purposely smashed.

A casket has been dug up and smashed opened. The remains of the deceased are scattered about and the thieves left nothing of value. The corpse's shattered jawbone suggests they might have been after gold teeth.

Beyond this southern border the Barrens of Crakamir extend for a great distance. There's nothing out there for you but certain death. Turn back, brave adventurer; you'll have to save those travels for another time.

Before you sits a crystal ball, an ancient tool of the Mystics, used for seeing into the past and the future. When you peer into it all you see is a swirling, cloudy mist. It fills you with a sense of dread until you look away.

This entry chamber seems to be a sort of "waiting room" where remains are stored until caretakers can move the bones deeper into the ossuary. With no one tending to the ossuary anymore, thieves have viscously raided this area, scattering bones everywhere. At the opposite side of the entry chamber is a doorway. Blood has been smeared across its threshold, a common warding practice meant to keep restless souls from exiting. It is also regarded as a warning sign for the living to stay away.
The larger inner chamber is an area of general bone storage. To the left and right sides of this long room are shelves packed tight with human remains.
Here, someone has smashed through a shelf and wall, revealing a hidden passage way!

This wall appears to be newer than the surrounding walls. Bricks and mortar on the ground leads you to believe that someone has recently sealed this passage. The wall feels solid and would take days to smash apart; you would be better off finding another way.
Although the sign recommends you wait for a crypt attendant, you very much doubt that anyone will come to greet you.
This small chamber looks to be a holding cell of sorts. Perhaps grave robbers, caught in the act, are secured here.

This building is a place of suffering and nightmares. Devices of torture lay about, as do human bones and scraps of clothing. A rancid cauldron of boiled-down fat adds a putrid stench to the air. Amid this horror you see a man hanging from a rack. He seems to still be alive.

This is the entrance to the Goblin's Citadel. Very few humans have seen past these dark walls, and those who have never returned to tell about it. To the northeast, the Citadel stands as a massive black monolith against the desert sky. From this vantage point you see that many goblins occupy the inner yard. Makeshift barricades protect archers and hackers, ready to charge anyone foolish enough to enter the gateway.
You realize that once you enter the gateway, all of hell will open up. You only hope that Omar holds true to his promise that the Giants will aid your entry into the Citadel.

The Goblins, aware that the Citadel is under assault, suddenly lock down every gateway and portcullis! You'll have to search for another way to reach the inner foyer and gain access to the next level.

Inside the Citadel the air is stagnant and thick with the putrid smell of goblins. Twisted corridors suggest a senseless and improvised method of construction. You must be cautious for there are undoubtedly dangers lurking in every shadow.

You have found a holding dungeon filled with the remains of at least a dozen humans, some of whom have been here for a very long time. They all appear to have been chained to the walls and tortured for reasons unknown.
This tomb has no ceiling. Far above, a reflector directs daylight down the long vertical shaft. It is enough to keep a small bit of grass and a couple trees alive in this place of death.

Yet another unfortunate casualty of this war: a simple homeowner murdered in his house, his head smashed open and everything of value taken. Bloody footprints throughout the house suggest a band of thugs committed this act within the last two days.
This hallway ends as an unfinished tunnel cut directly into rock.
This looks like the remains of a wagon caravan. It has been smashed into countless pieces.
This looks rather like a cave cut into the bedrock, but it has been reinforced with walls of brick and mortar. Concrete steps lead down into the darkness.

You approach the edge of the waterfall where the river plunges into the chasm with a deafening roar. You cannot see the bottom of the rift and have no idea how far the water must be falling. You imagine that with enough time the whole sea could eventually be swallowed by this abyss.
The outpost is dark and quiet. You find the lack of life unnerving- not a single beetle crawls across the sand covered floor, nor a single patch of mold grows on the walls.
This doorway looks as if it has been bricked and mortared shut. The wall is solid and you see no way of passing.
It seems very clear that this place has been raided and scavenged years ago. Nothing of value remains and every chest appears smashed open.
Before you even open the door, you can smell the pungent scent of a distiller in use. The air is saturated with the smell of fermenting grains and poor-quality alcohol.
Gramuk falls to the floor. His body writhes and his skin cracks. Amidst a shower of magickal energy, he transforms into a Dirachnid- a massive spider seen only in the deepest of dungeons!

With that final blow, the Dirachnid's body crumbles in a spray of gore. A blue mist pours from the broken shell of the giant spider and crawls through the air as if looking for refuge. You stand back and watch it dissipate until you are confident that the creature is truly dead, then you sense a calmness settle upon the room.

Contained within the yellowed pages of this tome is the text of one of the many religious faiths. The first pages describe the process of creation, as most holy books often do: *"Long ago, there were only the great ones- the Darkness, named Onos, and the Light, named Rai. They fought for control of the sky, but it was Onos who dominated and kept Rai away, exiled far beyond the most distant stars. In this time, Darkness reigned supreme." *"But Rai schemed to dethrone Onos and so gathered an army of burning comets for which to attack the darkness. From the black abyss of the most distant realm, Rai moved with his army and surprised Onos, driving back darkness and bringing light to the sky." *"Onos, in all his wickedness, retaliated with great vengeance! In an act of madness, he punched a hole in the sky to consume all of the comets, but their numbers were too great. As all of the cosmos began falling into this hole, the comets came crashing together and formed a single brilliant gem, too large to be pulled through the opening. The gem became known as Eschalon, and its greatness alone was enough to seal the hole formed by Onos." *"With the immense pull created by Eschalon and the remnant hole, Onos and Rai were dragged into an endless spiral from which they could not escape. Ever spinning around Eschalon, they gave the land its first day and night, which has continued for endless millennia since. Their imprisonment became the gift of all the creatures of Eschalon."

Gramuk leads you to a large vault just off the main vestibule in his tower room. In the vault you see huge chests filled with gold, gemstones, and priceless bars of Divine Ore. He picks up a canvas sack and begins scooping armfuls of neatly stacked coins from a table into it until the top can barely close. *"With the Crux back in our possession we now have the power to reclaim our ancient homelands. You've aided the race of Goblins, and now I make good on my offer." Gramuk lifts the hefty sack of gold and places it in your arms. "Take this gold, human. It is enough to buy passage out of Thaermore where you can retire as a wealthy lord. But heed this warning: once you leave this Citadel you will be just another human to us. Leave Thaermore and never return." *You cinch the sack of gold closed and hoist it onto your shoulder. It is heavy. Perhaps its weight is more than that of the gold alone, for you realize this sack represents the death of many humans. It represents the lands of Thaermore falling to the Goblin scourge. In time, the weight of this gold may be more than you can bear, but for now your only worry is getting out of Thaermore alive.

My dearest sister Penelope, *We have reached the Southern Gates only to find them sealed and with no way to pass into Thaermore. Our caravan leader assured us the gates would be passable, but now we are stuck in Crakamir. Some of the travelers want to return south, others want to stay and find a way north. Either way we are in grave danger if we remain here much longer. *I am writing you this letter in the hope that it reaches you. At daybreak we are going to send someone from the caravan to scout ahead and find a passage to Blackwater. I will give him this letter and instruct him to deliver it to you when he reaches Blackwater. *Sis, I am very fearful. All night we have heard sounds in the darkness. I think our caravan may be encircled, but by what I do not know. We keep the fires burning bright to scare off any creatures, but I think it may be attracting them. *-Mort-

Michael, priest man of Aridell: *You should have alembic and portal area prepared by now. The next task of portal construction requires Bromine and Ambergris to be placed in the alembic. There are two more elements to be added before portal will be ready. I will send further instructions soon. *-Gramuk
